rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall was extraordinarily high and thick, like a fortress wall; the narrative indicates it was miraculously set upright.
rows.anchor: bu bir kale duvarı gibi yüksek ve kalın bir duvar imiş

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some suppose Khidr demolished the wall and then rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: bazılarının zannettiği gibi ihtimal bunu yıkmış ve durup yeniden yapmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects demolition and rebuilding as the likely sense: even attempting to demolish a wall there would be extraordinary, so the wording implies a miraculous straightening.
rows.anchor: böyle bir memlekette, o garib vaziyette bir duvarı yıkmaya kalkışmak bile alelâde bir şey olamayacağı

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve İbn Cübeyr
rows.claim: They report that Khidr passed his hand over the wall and straightened it; al-Qurtubi calls this the sound view.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan ve İbn Cübeyr’den rivayet olunduğuna göre[^1] eliyle meshetmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa saw gratuitous charity as senseless when they urgently needed food and could have earned payment; he objected mildly this time and did not fear separation.
rows.anchor: bir sırada mümkin olan bir kesbi bırakıp fuzûlî bir teberru‘yapmaya kalkışmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr announces their parting and says he will explain the hidden meaning, purpose, and wisdom behind the ship, boy, and wall episodes that Musa could not patiently endure.
rows.anchor: gemi, oğlan, duvar hakkında yaptığım şeylerin sana hafî kalan meal ve maksadını, bâtındaki vech ü hikmetini anlatayım

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: One report identifies the king as Julanda son of Karker, ruler of Ghassan.
rows.anchor: Bu Gassan meliki Cülendâ b. Kerker idi denilmiş

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Another report identifies him as Mikvad son of al-Julband in al-Andalus.
rows.anchor: Endelüs cezîresinde Mikvad b. el-Cülbend idi denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tyrannical king seized every sound, unimpaired ship, so damaging this vessel was the lesser evil and helped its poor owners escape confiscation.
rows.anchor: sağlam, kusursuz olan her gemiyi gasbediyordu. Binâen‘aleyh gemiyi biraz yaralayıp ayıplandırmak, o gasbdan kurtarmak için ehven-i şerreyni ihtiyar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine rulings may look harmful on the surface but prove beneficial when their hidden wisdom is known.
rows.anchor: zâhiren zarar gibi görünen şeylere tesadüf olunur ki ledünniyâtı bilinirse onların zarar değil, menfaat olduğu tebeyyün eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy's parents were believers, and Khidr feared the boy would overwhelm them with rebellion and disbelief.
rows.anchor: Oğlana gelince: Ebeveyni iki mü’min idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that the boy was already mature, rebellious, and an unbeliever intent on bringing his parents under his influence.
rows.anchor: oğlan göründüğü gibi masum değil idi, bülûğa ermiş, azmış bir kâfir idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, although still a child, he was disposed to future unbelief and rebellion that would mislead his parents if he lived.
rows.anchor: Yahut henüz sabî ise de öyle küfr ü tuğyâna müsta‘id idi ki, sağ kalırsa ileride anasını babasını bile azıtacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parents' sincere faith made them deserving of divine protection from this evil, and the boy's childhood death was better for all concerned.
rows.anchor: o ana babanın imanlarındaki hulûsu min-tarafillah böyle bir şerden muhafaza olunmaya lâyık ve onun sabî iken ölmesi hepsi hakkında hayırlı idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would replace him with a child better in purity and closer in mercy, sparing the parents his harm and compensating their grief with a more beloved child.
rows.anchor: Hem oğlanın yüzünden görecekleri şerden kurtulacaklar, hem de onun ölümüyle duyacakları acıya mukabil daha sevimli bir evlâda nâil olacaklardı

rows.speaker: rivayet olunduğuna göre
rows.claim: A report says God gave the parents a daughter in his place; she became a prophet's mother, and a community was guided through that prophet.
rows.anchor: ona bedel Allah bunlara bir kız vermiş ve bu kız bir peygamber vâlidesi olmuş ve o peygamberin eliyle ümmetlerden bir ümmet hidâyete ermiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasure was apparently a cache of gold and silver, though another transmitted view calls it a gold tablet containing wisdom and admonitions.
rows.anchor: Yani bunlar için saklanmış bir altın ve gümüş definesi vardı. Bunun birtakım hikmet ve nesâyihi muhtevî bir altın levha olduğu da mervî ise de evvelkisi zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasure was the inheritance of a righteous father, lawfully earned and set aside with good intention for spending in God's cause, not the condemned hoard in 9:34.
rows.anchor: o define onlara sâlih bir babanın mirası idi, helâlinden kazanılmış ve fî-sebîlillah sarfolunmak için hüsn-i niyetle konmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphans benefit from their father's righteousness, not merely from being orphans.
rows.anchor: O iki yetim, yalnız yetim olduklarından dolayı değil, babalarının salâhından müstefid olarak o defineye nâil olacaklardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes their father as highly trustworthy: people entrusted him with deposits, and he returned them as received.
rows.anchor: Çok emin bir adamdı, nâs ona emanetler tevdî‘ederler, o da verdikleri gibi teslim ederdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserved the treasure until the two orphans reached maturity; had the wall fallen earlier, others would have found and taken it.
rows.anchor: Bunlar büyümeden duvar yıkılmış olsa idi o defineyi başkaları bulacak ve zâyi‘olacaktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's act was a mercy from God and a duty commanded by God, not an exercise of his own judgment.
rows.anchor: kendi re’y ü ictihâdımdan değil, Rabbinin bildirdiği emriyle O’nun bir rahmeti olmak üzere yaptım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Musa says nothing after the explanation, Elmalılı infers that he saw nothing in it to reject and understood that the apparently harmful acts had hidden reasons and wisdom.
rows.anchor: Demek ki Mûsâ’nın zâhiren muzır ve münker gördüğü şeyler hakikatte öyle değil imiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An apparent requirement of the hidden reality may differ from the apparent requirement of outward law, yet this does not make reality and revealed law conflict, since both are God's true judgment.
rows.anchor: muktezâ-yı bâtın, muktezâ-yı zâhire muhalif olabilir. Fakat bundan dolayı hakikatle şeriatın tehâlüfü lâzım gelmez

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı Rabbânî
rows.claim: In Maktubat I.43 he rejects antinomian claims that the ultimate aim lies beyond the Sharia: tariqa and Sharia are identical, and any claim of reality rejected by Sharia is heresy.
rows.anchor: tarikat ve şeriat birbirinin aynıdır. Aralarında kıl ucu kadar muhalefet yoktur, şeriata her muhalif olan merduddur

rows.speaker: İmâm-ı Rabbânî
rows.claim: In Maktubat I.41, refraining from a spoken lie is Sharia, removing its thought with effort is tariqa, and effortless removal is reality; the inner paths complete the outward law.
rows.anchor: dilin yalan söylememesi şeriat, kalbden yalan hâtırasını nefyetmek eğer tekellüf ve te‘ammül ile olursa tarikat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı raises the problem that killing a minor for future disbelief would violate Sharia, even if Khidr knew the child's future; Umar likewise refused to punish a man for a crime not yet committed.
rows.anchor: bir sabî şöyle dursun bir bâliği bile ileride yapacağı cürümden dolayı katletmek şüphe yok ki şer‘e muhaliftir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh
rows.claim: Umar said that although he knew Mughirah's slave would kill him, the man had done nothing yet and could not be punished merely for what was in his heart; the slave killed him the next day.
rows.anchor: henüz bir şey yapmamıştır ve sırf kalbindeki şeyden dolayı da şer‘an muâhaze olunmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed answer is that the boy was an adult, a rebellious unbeliever liable to execution, rather than the innocent child Musa assumed.
rows.anchor: onun نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةًۢ diye bir masum zannettiği oğlan sabî değil, bâliğ azgın bir kâfir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer is that Sharia is God's command and Khidr says he acted only by God's command, so he was a prophet under a special revelation and law for this case.
rows.anchor: Hızır ahvâl-i mahsûsada bir şerî‘at-i mahsûsa ile me’mur bir peygamber olduğunu anlatmış demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this explanation, the boy's execution differs from analogy but follows a special revealed law; the difference is between the laws of two prophets, not between Sharia and reality.
rows.anchor: iki peygamberin şeriatları beyninde bir farka râci‘olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's knowledge encompasses hidden causes, past secrets, and future destinies as though they were outwardly present; this is called knowledge of the unseen, inward knowledge, or, specifically, ladunni knowledge.
rows.anchor: Evvelâ; ilim nokta-i nazarından bakıldığı zaman onun ilmi gemi, gulâm, duvar hakkında olduğu gibi eşyânın mâverâ-yı şuhûdu olan ledünniyâtını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's acts proceed from God toward people as execution of divine decrees, rather than being acts that lead people toward God; killing the boy resembles the Angel of Death's assigned task.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ gibi halkı Hakk’a götürmeye me’mur değil, Hak’tan halka olan mukadderâtın infâzına me’mur demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the hidden causes were unknown, Khidr's deeds appeared ugly and unwise; once explained, two conform to analogy and one is an equitable exception against analogy.
rows.anchor: üçte ikisi kıyasa muvâfık ve biri alâ-hilâfi’l-kıyas bir istihsan olduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa came to learn guidance from Khidr's special knowledge, but the practical and legal commission he witnessed differed from his own and allowed no ordinary objection, making their separation necessary.
rows.anchor: cihet-i ameliye ve şer‘iyede kendisinin me’mûriyetine tevâfuk etmeyen ve bununla beraber itiraza da hak vermeyen husûsiyetler bulunduğunu öğrenmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musa was a prophet commissioned to proclaim and disclose, whereas Khidr was commissioned to act immediately.
rows.anchor: Demek ki Mûsâ, ilmini tebliğ ve izhâra me’mur ulü’l-azmden bir peygamber olduğu hâlde, Hızır tebliğe değil

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some hold that Khidr was a saint rather than a prophet.
rows.anchor: nebî değil, bir velî olduğuna kāil olanlar olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı argues that if Khidr were only a saint, he could not possess a special ruling authorizing the boy's killing.
rows.anchor: yalnız velî olsa idi oğlanı öldürmek için hükm-i mahsûsa sâhip olamazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story does not establish Khidr's superiority over Musa; it shows Musa was not all-comprehensive and lacked some ladunni knowledge.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle kıssa Hızır’ın Mûsâ’dan efdaliyetini iktizâ etmez. Ancak Mûsâ’nın câmi‘u’l-kül olmadığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story prepares the reader to understand the perfection of the Muhammadan station as combining the two prophets' distinct manifestations.
rows.anchor: Bu da hem Hızır’ın hem Mûsâ’nın mazhariyetlerini câmi‘bir zü’l-cenâheyn tasavvurunu telkin

rows.speaker: bazı rivayete göre
rows.claim: Some reports say the questioners about Dhul-Qarnayn were polytheists; other reports identify them as People of the Book, with Quraysh asking at the Jews' prompting.
rows.anchor: Soranlar, bazı rivayete göre müşrikler, diğer bazı rivayete göre ehl-i kitab idi

rows.speaker: Ukbe b. Âmir
rows.claim: Uqbah reports that People of the Book asked to question the Prophet; he initially said he knew only what God disclosed, then prayed and invited them to ask about Dhul-Qarnayn and matters in their scripture.
rows.anchor: Ukbe b. Âmir’den[^1] rivayet olunduğuna göre demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddi's report says Jews challenged Muhammad to tell of a figure mentioned only once in the Torah, and they named Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim’in[^2] Süddî’den tahrîcine göre Hazret-i Peygamber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn is a title like Dhu al-Yadayn and comparable to Dhu al-Janahayn; qarn can mean horn, era, contemporaneous people, head or temples, forelock, women's locks, sun's rim, or a people's chief.
rows.anchor: “karn” birçok mânalara gelir. Ezcümle boynuz, asır, bir zamanda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-known explanation, suggested by the Qur'an's account, is that the title means master of the earth's east and west, a world-conqueror.
rows.anchor: En meşhuru Kur’ân’ın beyânından da anlaşılacağı vechile Arz’ın şark u garbına sâhip demek olmasıdır

rows.speaker: Hüseyin Vâ‘iz
rows.claim: Husayn Waiz also interprets the title as mastery of outward and inward realities, expressed in Turkish as 'two-winged.'
rows.anchor: Hüseyin Vâ‘iz tefsirinde mezkur olduğu üzere zâhir ü bâtına sâhip mânası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More than one person was called Dhul-Qarnayn; the Quranic figure is distinguished as the Greater Dhul-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: lakabıyla telkīb edilmiş olan zevâtın bir değil, müte‘addid olduğu anlaşılıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Himyarite conquerors Sa'b and Shammar Yer'ash were called Dhul-Qarnayn; Feridun and Alexander were also given the title, later popularly associated with Alexander.
rows.anchor: Sa‘b ve Semerkand isminin nâmına nisbeti nakledilen

rows.speaker: Yehûd kitapları
rows.claim: A report about Jewish books describes Dhul-Qarnayn as a young man from Rome who built Egypt and Alexandria; some exegetes, including al-Alusi, therefore identify him as Alexander.
rows.anchor: kitaplarında Zülkarneyn Rumdan çıkan bir genç idi ki Mısır’ı ve İskenderiye’yi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı allows Alexander was one of those called Dhul-Qarnayn but rejects identifying him as the Quran's exalted figure: the Quranic great figures possess prophethood, and no historical barrier built by Alexander is known.
rows.anchor: makām-ı nübüvveti de hâiz bulunduğuna göre İskender’in bu derece yükseltilmesi şâyân-ı kabul görülmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Alexander was famous in later history and his story could be learned without revelation, his identity would not suit questioners testing prophethood; the subject must be more obscure.
rows.anchor: meşhur ve mâlum olduğu cihetle bunu peygambere sormak sâillerin garazına muvâfık olmazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Histories also record a Roman emperor's barrier in Britain and Nushirvan's barrier at the Caucasus site called the Iron Gate.
rows.anchor: Roma kayserlerinden birinin İngiltere’de, Kisrâ Nûşirevan’ın Kafkas dağlarında “Bâbü’l-ebvâb”, ta‘bîr-i âharla “Demirkapı” denilen mevki’de birer sed yapmış olduklarını tarihler gösteriyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A still older and greater conqueror such as Egyptian Ramses, said to have reached the Scythians and built a barrier from the Mediterranean to the Caspian, is a more plausible target of the question.
rows.anchor: Mısırlı büyük Ramses gibi maddî mânevî bir şöhreti hâiz bulunan daha eski ve daha yüksek bir cihangiri istihdaf etmiş olmak rivâyeten ve dirâyeten daha mülâyimdir

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify Dhul-Qarnayn as Feridun son Esfiyan son Jamshid, a just and virtuous ruler from ancient Persian tradition in Abraham's era.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunun İbrâhim aleyhisselâm zamanına müsâdif Afridun [Feridun] b. Esfiyan b. Cemşid olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Zeyd-i Belhî
rows.claim: Abu Zayd al-Balkhi says Feridun was supported by revelation, while historical accounts describe him as a great conqueror.
rows.anchor: Ebû Zeyd-i Belhî Suver-i Ekālîm nâmındaki kitabında Afridun’un vahiyle müeyyed olduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: İbn İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives Dhul-Qarnayn's name as Marziban son of Marduyah.
rows.anchor: İbn İshak Zülkarneyn’in ismi Merziban b. Merduye olduğunu söylemiş

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Other identifications name him as Abdullah son of Dahhak or Mus'ab son of Abdullah, tracing a long Himyarite genealogy.
rows.anchor: bazıları Abdullah b. Dahhâk demiş, bazıları da Mus‘ab b. Abdullah b. Feynan

rows.speaker: Ebû Reyhân Bîrûnî
rows.claim: Al-Biruni identifies Dhul-Qarnayn as the Himyarite Abu Karb Sumay son of Ubayd son of Afrikish, whose realm reached the earth's eastern and western regions.
rows.anchor: Ebû Reyhân Bîrûnî el-Âsâru’l-bâkiye ani’l-kurûni’l-hâliye nâm eserinde

rows.speaker: Himyerî şâiri
rows.claim: A Himyarite poet's verses boast that his Muslim grandfather Dhul-Qarnayn reached east and west seeking the means of kingship from a wise guide.
rows.anchor: قَدْ كَانَ ذُو الْقَرنَينِ جَدِّي مُسْلِماً مَلِكاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Himyarite identification seems likelier because other rulers bearing the 'Dhu' titles were Yemenite, and Afrikish was a known Himyarite ruler associated with Africa.
rows.anchor: Zûyezen, Zûceden gibi “zû’lar hep Yemen’dendir” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes the reported descendant Abu Karb Sumay or Shams ibn Umayr cannot be verified historically; the name may be corrupted from Shammer Yer'ash.
rows.anchor: nâmında birisi târihen tesbit olunamamış ve binâen‘aleyh Ebû Reyhan’ın nakline itiraz edilip

rows.speaker: rivayette
rows.claim: One report says Shammer, son of Afrikish, marched toward Iraq and China, erected inscriptions, and founded Samarkand; the poet Dibbil celebrates these deeds.
rows.anchor: Şemmer Efrîkış’ın oğlu olup Irak ve Çin’e doğru hareket ederek vardığı yerlerde kitabeler diktirdiği

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some say Shammer was named Dhul-Qarnayn because he wore two braids; the stronger account makes him son of Nasir al-Ni'am and later than Solomon's Queen of Sheba, too late to be the Quranic figure.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu Şemmer’in başında iki saç örgüsü olduğundan dolayı

rows.speaker: Ebü’l-Fidâ
rows.claim: Abu al-Fida identifies him as Sa'b son of Rayish, and transmits Ibn Abbas's identification of the Quranic Dhul-Qarnayn as the Himyarite Sa'b, not Alexander.
rows.anchor: Ebü’l-Fidâ Târîhi’nde der ki: “Zülkarneyn, Râyiş’in oğlu Sa‘b’dır

rows.speaker: Kāmûs mütercimi Âsım Efendi
rows.claim: Asim Efendi supports Sa'b's identification in his discussion of the word Alexander and adds further details.
rows.anchor: Âsım Efendi de “İskender” kelimesinde bu kavli teyid ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traditions placing both Sa'b and Feridun in Abraham's time are difficult to reconcile; Himyar and the Tubba' dynasty are plausible origins, but the Quranic figure's identity remains historically uncertain.
rows.anchor: bunların tedkīki müşkil olduğu gibi, Kur’an’da zikrolunan Zülkarneyn’in bunlardan o unvânı almış birisi mi

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: Following al-Suhayli, Elmalılı prefers the safest report: Dhul-Qarnayn was a righteous servant who loved God and was loved by God.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den rivayet olunan şu fıkrada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Identifying the figure's personal name is unnecessary and contrary to the Quranic emphasis: the question concerns his title, and the answer recalls the story explaining its significance.
rows.anchor: Zira sual, Zülkarneyn vasfı üzere îrad edilmiş olduğu gibi, cevapta da ismi ve şahsiyetin tâyinine taarruz olunmayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established Dhul-Qarnayn in the earth and made material and spiritual powers available to him.
rows.anchor: maddî mânevî kuvvetleri, kudretleri müheyyâ kıldık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him every means needed to reach his aims, including knowledge, power, tools, and resources; he acted through means, whose efficacy is assigned by God rather than intrinsic.
rows.anchor: zâhir ü bâtından ilim, kudret, âlât ve vesâit gibi her türlü esbâbı ihsan eyledik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn followed a means westward until the far western edge of the inhabited earth, reaching the Atlantic Ocean.
rows.anchor: Bahr-ı Muhît-i Garbî’nin (Atlasî) kenarına erdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators locate his destination at the Atlantic; the Fortunate Isles were once used as the origin for longitude, though their identity is now unknown.
rows.anchor: Bu okyanus denizinde “Halidat” nâmı verilen cezâirin bir zamanlar mebde’-i tûl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes read hami'a as muddy and the alternate hamiya reading as hot; they identify the spring as water and the setting point as the ocean horizon.
rows.anchor: “hami’e”yi balçıklı, “hâmiye”yi de kızgın mânasına tefsir etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the shore, the sun seemed to sink into a dark, muddy, steaming basin, a visual impression shaped by the ocean and horizon.
rows.anchor: Bu surette bu su gözünden murad, bahr-ı muhît ve ale’l-husûs denizin ufuktaki gurûb noktasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The setting sun's impression teaches that worldly dominion has limits and is transient.
rows.anchor: dünya şevketinin mahdûdiyetini görmek ve fânîliğini anlamaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says God's address, 'We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn,' clearly indicates that Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet.
rows.anchor: Bu kavil, doğrusu Zülkarneyn’in nübüvvetinde zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although free to punish or treat the people well, Dhul-Qarnayn assigns punishment to wrongdoers and reward to believers who do good, avoiding misuse of power because he knows he will return to God.
rows.anchor: ta‘zîbi zulmedenlere, ihsan ve mükâfâtı da iman edip amel-i sâlih yapanlara tahsis etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After his western campaign he followed a route eastward, reaching the point where the sun rises without an intervening barrier.
rows.anchor: garbda gurûb eden Güneş’in şarka dönmesi gibi mağribden maşrıka giden bir yol peşine düştü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eastern destination might be Africa's east coast, but the more apparent interpretation is the far east of Asia.
rows.anchor: bu nokta Afrika’nın sâhil-i şarkīsi olmak muhtemil ise de zâhir olan Asya’nın aksâ-yı şarkı olmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He interprets the people as lacking buildings and clothes and being exposed to the sun, like naked groups then known in Sudan and Australia; in customary terms, only substantial shelter counts, so the description can also fit many desert nomads.
rows.anchor: ebniyeleri yok, hatta elbiseleri yok, Güneş’in altında yanıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew everything in Dhul-Qarnayn's possession: He had supplied him with abundant means but gave the sun-exposed people no means of shelter.
rows.anchor: Zülkarneyn’in mülkünde o kadar çok esbâb ü vesâit vardı ki tamamını ancak Allah biliyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also knows what Dhul-Qarnayn felt and did when he encountered those people.
rows.anchor: bunları gördüğü zaman Zülkarneyn’in ne hisler duyduğunu, ne işler yaptığını da Allah bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From west to east, Dhul-Qarnayn then traveled either south or north; the commentators' descriptions suggest he went north.
rows.anchor: Ki bu da ya cenûba veya şimâle olabilir. Ma‘amâfîh müfessirînin ifadelerine nazaran şimâle gitti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sadd is something that securely closes a gap; a barrier between things is called a sadd, and the word also applies to a mountain.
rows.anchor: “Seddetmek” bir şeyin gediğini sağlam kapamaktır. İki şey arasına hâil olan hâcize “sed” denildiği gibi dağa dahi ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some distinguish the readings with damma for a natural barrier and fatha for a human-made one; others distinguish visible from invisible barriers, though the author allows the readings may convey further nuances.
rows.anchor: “sin”in zammıyla “süd”, sun‘-i beşerle yapılana da feth ile “sed” deniliyor demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two barriers might be artificial, or natural features such as seas, continents, or mountains, and could be visible or invisible; exegetes identify them as mountains but cannot fix which mountains.
rows.anchor: iki sed, sun‘î iki mâni‘a olabileceği gibi iki deniz, iki kıt‘a-i arz, iki dağ gibi hılkī, yahut mer’î ve gayr-i mer’î de olabilecektir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Ebussuud
rows.claim: One location places the mountains where the land of the Turks ends to the north and east; if that means Transoxiana, it points to the Great Wall of China.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî ve Ebussuud buna itimad etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Kâdî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Baydawi favors a location where Turkestan ends beside Armenia and Azerbaijan, identifying the mountains with the Caucasus and the pass with Darband, where Nushirvan built a barrier.
rows.anchor: Kâdî Beyzâvî bunu tercih etmek istemiştir. Bu kavle göre bu dağlar Kafkas dağları ve “beyne’s-seddeyn” Demirkapı mevki‘i oluyor

rows.speaker: Ebû Reyhan
rows.claim: Biruni says the location should lie in the northwestern quarter of the inhabited world.
rows.anchor: Ebû Reyhan demiştir ki bu mevzi‘in, ma‘mûreden şimâl-i garbî rub‘unda olması iktizâ ediyor

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: A third proposal places two great mountains in the far north, called 'Jirbiya' in Ezekiel, a name reminiscent of Siberia; possible ranges include the Urals, Stanovoy, Caucasus, or Kamchatka, but the Quran does not settle the location.
rows.anchor: Şimâlin âhirlerinde iki cebel-i münîf ki Hazkıyal aleyhisselâm’ın kitabında “âhirü’l-cirbiyâ” denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best-known barriers are China's Wall in the east and Bab al-Abwab in the west; this would put the pass between them in Turkestan and accord with reports about the people encountered there.
rows.anchor: şarkta Sedd-i Çin garbda Bâbü’l-ebvâb mâruf olduğuna göre iki sedden murad bunlar olmak daha zâhirdir denilebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people could scarcely understand or convey speech: their language was strange and expression limited, and without God's provision of means Dhul-Qarnayn could not communicate with them.
rows.anchor: Dilleri garib, ifadeleri kāsırdı. Zülkarneyn’e her şeyden bir sebep verilmemiş olsaydı bunlara söz anlatamayacak

rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Although the Quran does not identify the people, exegetes traditionally report that they were Turks, who would help Dhul-Qarnayn build the barrier against Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bunun hangi kavim olduğunu tasrih etmemiştir. Fakat müfessirîn, Türk denilmiş olduğunu nakledegelmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people describe Gog and Magog as corrupters who devastate everything before them and would ruin the whole earth if left unchecked.
rows.anchor: Yani işleri Arz’ı ifsad etmektir. Bu Arz’ı berbat ediyorlar, önlerine geleni tahrib eyliyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names Ya'juj and Ma'juj are loanwords from another language; westerners call them Yagug and Magug, regard them as Satan's offspring, and applied the names to the Huns invading the Western Roman Empire.
rows.anchor: “Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc” yahut “Yâcûc ve Mâcûc” isimleri

rows.speaker: bazı tefsirler
rows.claim: Some exegetical works recount the People of the Book's myth that Gog and Magog arose from Adam's nocturnal emission, whereas Genesis identifies Gog as a son of Japheth.
rows.anchor: ehl-i kitabdan bazılarının Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’u Hazret-i Âdem’in bir ihtilâmından husûle gelmişler diye bir efsane naklettiklerini

rows.speaker: Vehb b. Münebbih ve daha bazı zevat
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih and others assert that Gog and Magog are two tribes descended from Japheth, a view many later writers trust.
rows.anchor: Vehb b. Münebbih ve daha bazı zevat, Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’un evlâd-ı Yâfes’ten iki kabile olduklarına cezmetmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses the plural 'corrupters' rather than a dual verb, suggesting great numbers; some say twenty tribes, while others say they form nine-tenths of humanity.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da tesniye ile “yüfsidâni” denilmeyip de “müfsidûne” denilmesi kesretlerine işaret olmak gerektir

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says none of the reports about Gog and Magog's number or appearance is sound.
rows.anchor: Bunların aded ve eşkâli hakkındaki sözlerin hiçbiri haber-i sahih değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In common Islamic usage, Gog and Magog means an ethnically obscure human mixture that recognizes neither religion nor nation; their emergence is among the signs of the Hour.
rows.anchor: Aslı ve nesebi belirsiz, din ve millet tanımaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compensation offer for building the barrier can be read with either fatha or damma on the initial sīn.
rows.anchor: Burada dahi sîn’in fethiyle de zammıyla da kıraat vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn says God's empowerment and station are better than their proposed payment, and he can build what they need voluntarily with greater ability than they imagined.
rows.anchor: Min-tarafillah bulunduğum makam, kuvve-i mâliye ve esbâb-ı sâire itibariyle sizin tasavvur ettiğiniz mertebeden daha yüksek ve daha nâfi‘dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks them for practical help with people, workers, craftsmen, tools, and equipment rather than money.
rows.anchor: mâlî masrafa karışmayınız da adamla, amele, sanatkâr, âlât ve edevât tedarikinde emrime âmâde olarak fiilen yardım ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A radm is a larger, stronger, more solid barrier than a sadd; because the people lie beyond the two passes and Gog and Magog farther beyond them, the barrier must be built beyond the two mountains.
rows.anchor: bir redim yapayım yani sedden daha muhkem bir şey, daha büyük daha metin bir gergi
